detail.abstract: Price indices constitute one of the most fundamental and extensively studied instruments in economics, serving as the primary tool for measuring inflation, adjusting nominal values, and informing monetary and fiscal policy. This paper provides a comprehensive survey of price index theory, tracing its evolution from the early contributions of Laspeyres (1871) and Paasche (1874) through Fisher's seminal The Making of Index Numbers (1922) to the modern superlative index theory of Diewert (1976). We examine the major classes of price indices—classical fixed-weight indices, superlative indices, continuous-time indices, and macroeconomic indicators—analyzing their respective advantages, limitations, and domains of application. Particular attention is devoted to the sources of bias inherent in traditional index formulations, including substitution bias, quality adjustment bias, and new goods bias, and to the methodological innovations—hedonic regression, scanner data integration, and chain-weighting—that have substantially improved index accuracy in recent decades. The paper concludes with an assessment of emerging challenges posed by the digital economy and directions for future research.

title: Quantum Bayesian Computation II: Posterior Functionals, Transport, and the Speed-Up Ledger
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business, George Mason University and University of Chicago, Students

detail.title: Quantum Bayesian Computation II: Posterior Functionals, Transport, and the Speed-Up Ledger
detail.abstract: Quantum Bayesian Computation (Polson et al., 2023) proposed von Neumann measurement as the evaluator of the large sums that Bayesian learning requires. This sequel revises the framework along three axes. First, we move from state vectors to density matrices and channels, where the theory belongs: latent variables are ancillae, data augmentation is purification, and integration is the partial trace. We show that the Petz recovery map is the non-commutative Bayes rule, reducing exactly to π(θ | y) ∝ p(y | θ)π(θ) on commuting algebras, and that fidelity restricted to commuting states is the Hellinger affinity, so the natural quantum training objective is one Bayesians already use. Second, we replace posterior sampling by posterior functional estimation. No-cloning forbids storing or reusing a prepared state and tomography costs Θ(d 2 /ϵ 2) copies, but Bayesian decision theory requires only a few functionals, and amplitude estimation supplies those at the Heisenberg rate ϵ-1 rather than the Monte Carlo rate ϵ-2. The same factor of two in the exponent reappears as the quantum Cramér-Rao and van Trees bounds, which identify it as the effect of entanglement across repetitions. Third, we identify state preparation as measure transport: the Grover-Rudolph circuit is the inverse Rosenblatt map executed in superposition, so that triangular transports, and only those, admit circuit analogues. We derive a crossover condition ϵ ≲ σ g /r in which the binding quantity is the compilation overhead r rather than the dimension, correct the Markov chain claim of the first paper via Szegedy dilation, read device noise as shrinkage toward the uniform prior, and close with a resource-counted ledger that separates the exponential claims from the quadratic ones.

title: De-dollarisation and the Future of Dollar Hegemony: Evaluating the Challenge from BRICS, the Chinese Renminbi and Alternative Financial Infrastructures

detail.title: De-dollarisation and the Future of Dollar Hegemony: Evaluating the Challenge from BRICS, the Chinese Renminbi and Alternative Financial Infrastructures
detail.abstract: This study evaluates whether the U.S. dollar's long-standing dominance is facing a structural challenge from the expanded BRICS bloc, China's currency strategy, and emerging cross-border payment infrastructures. As Western powers increasingly leverage financial networks and sanctions as tools of foreign policy, non-Western economies actively seek alternatives to insulate themselves from geopolitical risks and U.S. monetary policy spillovers. We analyze China's strategy of RMB internationalization, which deliberately prioritizes trade settlement platforms such as the Cross-Border Interbank Payment System (CIPS), petroyuan pricing, and digital currency mechanisms over full capital account liberalization. We show that while this "trade-first" strategy allows Beijing and its partners to bypass Western sanctions, strict domestic capital controls and shallow offshore RMB bond markets continue to restrict the currency's ability to serve as a major global store of value. Furthermore, while BRICS-led initiatives successfully expand local currency clearing, their systemic impact remains constrained by economic asymmetries and political divergences among member states. Rather than a sudden collapse of dollar hegemony, our findings point to a gradual fragmentation of the international monetary system, characterized by parallel financial architectures, higher transaction costs, and rising regional currency spheres.

detail.abstract: This method article validates a transparent multi-criteria decision framework for comparing green and secure logisticshub candidates in Egypt. Eight named candidate regions were evaluated on nine synthetic benefit and cost criteria covering connectivity, market and port access, intermodal potential, reverse logistics, security, resilience, emissions, and land cost. Balanced TOPSIS ranked Damietta first (score=0.573), followed by Beni Suef and Qena. However, rankings changed materially under a market-efficiency weighting scenario, while green-heavy, security-resilience, balanced, and entropy-derived rankings were more strongly correlated. The exercise validates data transformation, weighting, TOPSIS scoring, and sensitivity-analysis steps. It does not provide an investment recommendation because all criterion values are synthetic and approximate candidate labels do not represent surveyed sites.

title: The Alchemy of Fungible Money: A Trilateral Approach to Bridging Heterogeneities
affiliations: University of Newcastle (Australia) and

detail.title: The Alchemy of Fungible Money: A Trilateral Approach to Bridging Heterogeneities
detail.abstract: This paper examines why different forms of money-in the form of IOUs such as banknotes, commercial bank deposits, e-money and stablecoins-are generally treated as mutually interchangeable at face value (or "fungible") even though they are issued by different entities and carry different risks. It argues that perfect fungibility is not absolute, but is in fact illusory and thus akin to alchemy as means of payments in reality exhibit heterogeneities. The paper shows how heterogeneities are bridged in practice through numerous legal, operational, institutional, and psychological mechanisms that make heterogeneous IOUs appear as homogeneous to end-users. To this end, the paper argues that fungibility is not natural or permanent, but is socially, legally and institutionally produced and sustained. It goes on to present a hierarchical trilateral framework for understanding fungible money, consisting of fundamental, enabling and supportive elements. It also considers how declining cash use may influence perceptions of fungibility and suggests that public authorities-especially central banks-remain essential catalysts for preserving fungibility and therefore broad acceptance across a wide variety of payment instruments. Finally, the paper asserts that emerging forms of potential digital money in the form of stablecoins and tokenised deposits will need similar mechanisms if they are to become fully fledged means of payments.

detail.abstract: We build a novel property-level database of U.S. datacenter mortgages, an opaque AI-buildout financing channel. Linking mortgages to lender balance sheets, we document a large, concentrated market dominated by originate-to-distribute (OTD) banks and Undiversified Datacenter borrowers, whose repayment depends on continued AI demand rather than diversified revenue. Across complementary identification strategies, we find that the High-OTD leverage gap widens more than fourfold and that High-OTD lenders disproportionately finance these borrowers. Moreover, the leverage premium itself concentrates among Undiversified Datacenter borrowers, linking distribution incentives to looser underwriting and greater exposure to AI-demand risk.

title: The One-Way Valve: Crowdsourced Authenticity Flagging, Assistive Technology, and Disability Discrimination on the Professional Platform

detail.title: The One-Way Valve: Crowdsourced Authenticity Flagging, Assistive Technology, and Disability Discrimination on the Professional Platform
detail.abstract: On July 30, 2026, LinkedIn shipped a report option labeled "Seems like AI slop," inviting members to flag posts that read as machine-made, reducing the distribution of flagged posts, and feeding the flags into the platform's classifiers as training signal. This Article identifies the instrument's defining defect: it is a one-way valve. It collects accusations and nothing else. No countervailing judgment enters, ground truth never enters, and the resulting classifier learns complaint prevalence rather than authorship. The empirical record supplies each layer of the resulting injury. Humans cannot reliably distinguish machine text from human text, and their confidence bears no relation to their accuracy; crowd raters carry measured demographic biases that trained models absorb and amplify; evaluators penalize disclosed AI assistance even where the work is accurate and the author is human; and the writers most likely to be flagged write in the disciplined registers associated with disability, second-language acquisition, and assistive technology. The Article then maps the doctrine: disparate impact and meaningful access under the Americans with Disabilities Act and Section 504, the surcharge prohibition as applied to paid reach restoration, a procedural modification remedy that requires no alteration of any third party's content, and the resulting path through Section 230 in every circuit configuration, including the Fifth Circuit's July 2026 holding that the statutory shield and the First Amendment shield stack.

detail.abstract: Studies of the sovereign ceiling measure the constraint on private borrowers with the sovereign credit rating. S&P states that the operative cap is a separate assessment, the transfer and convertibility (T&C) assessment, which for most countries sits above the sovereign foreign-currency rating. I assemble a dated panel of S&P sovereign foreign-currency ratings, local-currency ratings and T&C assessments for 151 sovereigns and show that the two measures move together only partially. Across 711 one notch or larger sovereign rating changes between 2005 and 2025, pass-through into the ceiling is 0.902 for investment-grade sovereigns with their own currency, 0.443 for speculative grade sovereigns, and 0.030 for members of a monetary union. Merging the panel with BIS international debt securities data, private international issuance responds to the gap between the ceiling and the sovereign rating, while sovereign issuance responds to neither. One additional notch of headroom is associated with a cumulative increase of 0.473 log points in private gross issuance over three quarters.

title: The CEC Classification Framework: A Primary-Source Approach to Institutional Risk Measurement (Version 1)

detail.title: The CEC Classification Framework: A Primary-Source Approach to Institutional Risk Measurement (Version 1)
detail.abstract: This report documents the classification framework used to construct narrative-based nonmarket risk indices in a series of applied papers on institutional signaling and firm behavior. The framework, designated CEC (Coercion-Exchange-Cooperation), operationalizes a tri-dimensional typology of institutional interaction recovered from primary government communications via a fine-tuned ModernBERT-large classifier. The trained artifact is a four-class DIME (Diplomatic-Informational-Military-Economic) classifier; CEC drops the Informational class and reinterprets the remaining three as actor-agnostic signaling dimensions. The report documents the corpus (84,918 labeled documents from eight state and supranational origins), annotation protocol, and training configuration; reports performance on a 12,738-document test set (DIME accuracy 0.849, macro-F1 0.805; CEC macro-F1 0.841); presents an empirical case for the DIME→CEC reduction grounded in the model's error structure; and argues for CEC as a domain-appropriate replacement for borrowed taxonomies in institutional risk measurement. A keyword-dictionary baseline built from the annotation surfacing term lists attains at best accuracy 0.618 and macro-F1 0.439, with 62.5% of test documents matching no category's vocabulary decisively, quantifying the gain from contextual representation. Labels derive from a disclosed model-assisted protocol: generative-model candidates verified by a single expert annotator. On a balanced 5,376-document calibration set, model candidates agreed with hand labels in 85.1% of cases (𝜅 = 0.80), Informational at 65.6% concordance versus 87-96% for substantive classes-a pre-training signal of the residual-category structure the report documents. A successor, CECv2, with a multi-annotator protocol and expanded taxonomy is under development; this report fixes the artifact as a citable reference.

title:
Taxing Wealth: Take Half, Slowly

The Z-Tax - A Cash-Flow Tax to Tax Wealth and Economic Rents

detail.title:
Taxing Wealth: Take Half, Slowly

The Z-Tax - A Cash-Flow Tax to Tax Wealth and Economic Rents
detail.abstract: Governments are grappling with difficult issues in capital income tax, which is a mess, and with rising wealth inequality, with many suggestions for wealth taxation. Most proposals for wealth taxes are impractical-much wealth can't be valued; the taxes are unsupported by cash flows; the wealthy would leave, etc.. Worse, most such proposals worsen the income tax's over-taxation of savings, which reduces incentives to save and invest. I argue that a large consumption tax can, during the long transition, fall very heavily on wealth, and do so only as assets are realised or passed on. Savings previously made under an income/wage tax are taxed as they are consumed; this is classic 'double taxation' and is the same as taxing wealth once. Land taxation is another form of wealth tax as the tax reduces land values. This tax can be phased in to freeze house prices. This Z-tax (cash-flow) system taxes wealth slowly but heavily: total wealth in this country is, over time, more than halved. It then taxes only economic rents (super profits), and this transition is automatic.

title: Instrument-Free Endogeneity Correction beyond the Gaussian Copula: A Vine Approach with Identification

detail.title: Instrument-Free Endogeneity Correction beyond the Gaussian Copula: A Vine Approach with Identification
detail.abstract: Instrument-free copula corrections have become a standard response to endogenous regressors, yet every one of them fixes the dependence between the endogenous regressors and the structural error a priori, and fixes it as Gaussian. We relax it. The influence of the exogenous regressors is removed by a conditional rather than a marginal probability integral transform, leaving the dependence among the regressors entirely unrestricted; the remaining regressor-error dependence is modelled by a regular vine copula whose bivariate building blocks range over a comprehensive catalogue of families, symmetric and asymmetric, tail-dependent and tail-free. Vine structure, families, copula parameters and regression coefficients are estimated jointly in a single penalized maximum likelihood step, so the dependence is selected by the data rather than specified by the researcher. We prove point identification for any number of endogenous regressors, any vine structure and any conditioning depth, of the coefficients and of the dependence structure itself, under a condition that is checkable from data and that we show to be sharp. In retail scanner data the estimator recovers endogeneity that is state-dependent, and turns the dependence structure from a maintained assumption into an estimate a manager can read: which way a naive elasticity errs, and in which weeks the error concentrates.

title: Bayesian Volatility Modelling and Machine Learning Forecasting in Global Energy and Agricultural Commodity Markets: A Probabilistic Framework for Dynamic Dependence Analysis
affiliations: Gregory University Uturu, Abia State, Nigeria and

detail.title: Bayesian Volatility Modelling and Machine Learning Forecasting in Global Energy and Agricultural Commodity Markets: A Probabilistic Framework for Dynamic Dependence Analysis
detail.abstract: Forecasting the dynamic relationships among commodity markets is essential for effective portfolio management, risk diversification, and policy formulation. This study examines the volatility dynamics and time-varying dependence between global energy and agricultural commodity markets by integrating Bayesian stochastic volatility (SV) modelling, the Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC) model, and machine learning forecasting techniques. Daily returns for Brent crude oil, natural gas, wheat, corn, and soybean from January 2010 to December 2025 were analyzed. The Bayesian SV model was employed to estimate latent volatility, while the DCC model captured the evolving conditional correlations among commodity returns. The resulting dynamic correlations were subsequently forecast using Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. Forecast performance was evaluated using the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and the Diebold-Mariano test. The findings reveal persistent time-varying volatility across all commodity markets and stronger dynamic dependence among agricultural commodities than between energy and agricultural markets. Among the competing forecasting models, XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy, outperforming both Random Forest and LSTM across all evaluation metrics. The Diebold-Mariano test further confirmed that the forecasting improvements of XGBoost were statistically significant. These findings demonstrate that combining Bayesian stochastic volatility modelling with machine learning techniques provides a robust framework for modelling and forecasting dynamic commodity market dependence, offering valuable insights for investors, portfolio managers, and policymakers in commodity risk management.

title: The Pricing of Climate Talk in Listed Real Estate: Value or Values?

detail.title: The Pricing of Climate Talk in Listed Real Estate: Value or Values?
detail.abstract: I study the pricing of climate exposure for U.S. listed real estate firms from 2003 to 2024. Exposure measures the share of manager-analyst earnings-call exchanges devoted to climate-related topics. Firm-specific broad climate exposure predicts lower excess returns and is associated with lower implied cost of equity. The high-minus-low exposure portfolio earns a spread of around-3.9% over 12 months. Disaggregating this relation, positive and opportunity-oriented discussions produce the clearest lower-required-return evidence, whereas physical risk-related discussion yields opposing signals. Turning to concern-related revaluation, broad positive climate portfolios respond positively to climate concern shocks; regulatory-positive portfolios gain relative value most consistently when concern rises unexpectedly. Return-news tests reveal no general discount-rate channel for broad positive discussion. Under investor-focused climate news, concern shocks are associated with downward expected-return revisions for regulatory-positive and physical-positive portfolios, while opportunity-positive portfolios exhibit offsetting cash-flow and discount-rate news.

title: Quantifying Progress toward SDG 15: Empirical Pathways to Halt Land Degradation and Biodiversity Loss

detail.title: Quantifying Progress toward SDG 15: Empirical Pathways to Halt Land Degradation and Biodiversity Loss

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a review of published literature. It involved no human participants, no animal subjects, and no primary data collection, and therefore required no ethical approval.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Sustainable Development Goal 15 is measured by an indicator architecture that produces numbers reviewers and negotiators treat as observations of the world. Those numbers disagree with each other, sometimes by a factor of four within a single country. This integrative review asks where the disagreement originates and what follows for the empirical claim that progress toward SDG 15 can be quantified. Searches across fifteen query lanes in July 2026, covering OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and a full-text scholarly corpus, returned the evidence base synthesised here: 35 verified sources covering indicator 15.3.1 and its three sub-indicators, land degradation neutrality reporting, Earth observation evidence on degradation and tree cover, biodiversity trend indicators, and quasi-experimental evaluations of interventions. Two camps are read against each other. One treats divergence between estimates as a data problem that better sensors, finer resolution and national datasets will close; the other treats headline indicator values as artefacts of index construction. Neither position explains the pattern in the published estimates. A four-link measurement chain is proposed instead, separating the estimand, the observation, the aggregation rule and the attribution step, and the review locates the dominant source of divergence at each link. The largest published discrepancies trace to the estimand and the aggregation rule rather than to sensor quality, which means additional observation will not converge them. Reporting practice should carry sub-indicator results and the definitions that generated them alongside every headline figure.

title: Zakat On Trade Goods Between the Shafi'i and Hanbali Schools

detail.title: Zakat On Trade Goods Between the Shafi'i and Hanbali Schools
detail.abstract:
Zakat stands as the third pillar of Islam, representing a devotional obligation that bridges spiritual worship with ethical and economic dimensions. Scriptural texts firmly establish its status, notably the Hadith of Abdullah bin Omar (may Allah be pleased with them both) where the Prophet ﷺ stated: "Islam is built upon five..." including "giving Zakat." Almighty Allah commanded its collection to purify souls and uplift society, saying: "Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow in goodness."
Trade represents the backbone of economic vitality and wealth circulation, serving as the broadest avenue for profit encouraged by Islamic law. Because commerce relies on rotating capital for profit, Allah prescribed Zakat on trade goods to maintain social equilibrium. This duty safeguards the rights of the poor, prevents the hoarding of idle wealth, and stimulates the economy by incentivizing investors to keep capital productive.

title: The Effects of County-Level Naloxone Distribution on Drug Usage and Health Outcomes: Evidence from Indiana

detail.title: The Effects of County-Level Naloxone Distribution on Drug Usage and Health Outcomes: Evidence from Indiana

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: Vanderbilt Center for Research on Inequality and Health.

detail.abstract: Naloxone — a drug which can reverse an opioid overdose — has become a cornerstone of opioid harm-reduction policy, yet little is known about how institutional supply expansions affect public health, particularly in the fentanyl era. I study a statewide Indiana grant program that distributed naloxone kits to county health departments, providing the first evidence on this increasingly common distribution model. Using administrative data from 2014-2019 on naloxone kit distributions, emergency medical service (EMS) runs, health outcomes, and crime outcomes, I exploit staggered county participation in the program in a difference-indifferences framework to estimate the causal effect of the policy. I provide new first-stage evidence that program participation significantly increases naloxone administrations by 36.02%. Despite this, I find no improvements to opioid-related mortality and drug-related ED visits and hospitalizations. Using novel data on decedents' prior social services usage, I find strong evidence for a survival-reuse dynamic in which naloxone saves lives in the short run but survivors return to drug use and ultimately die: county participation in the program is associated with an 83.56% increase in the share of overdose decedents who had previously interacted with EMS. Further, opioid-related crime increases by 16.81%, consistent with increased drug-related activity. These results provide important insight into harm reduction policies during the fentanyl wave of the opioid epidemic and suggest that institutional naloxone distribution can successfully increase naloxone usage but that population-level health improvements require complementary interventions that reduce the risk of future overdose among survivors.

title: Synergies and Trade-offs in Implementing SDG 15: Evaluating Terrestrial Ecosystem Restoration Frameworks

detail.title: Synergies and Trade-offs in Implementing SDG 15: Evaluating Terrestrial Ecosystem Restoration Frameworks

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study did not involve human participants or animals. No ethical approval was required
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding

detail.abstract: Two bodies of evidence disagree about whether pursuing SDG 15 helps or obstructs the rest of the 2030 Agenda. Statistical studies of national indicator series report that synergies dominate the interaction network; expert elicitation and programme-level case evidence report trade-offs against poverty reduction, food security and water. This integrative review treats the disagreement as informative rather than as measurement noise, and argues that the design of terrestrial restoration frameworks determines where an interaction becomes visible and who absorbs it. Drawing on 36 sources retrieved through structured searches of OpenAlex and Consensus in July 2026, the paper compares four frameworks (forest landscape restoration under the Bonn Challenge, the Land Degradation Neutrality response hierarchy, Target 2 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, and the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration) across four design parameters: the degradation baseline, the accounting unit and counterbalancing scale, the holder of the commitment, and the success metric. Each parameter opens a channel through which a trade-off is displaced spatially, temporally, across sectors, or onto a different group rather than resolved. Four propositions state these relationships in testable form. The reconciliation follows from them: aggregate indicator studies sample the system after displacement, place-based studies sample it at the point of incidence, and both report correctly on what they observe. Frameworks that widen the counterbalancing scale without widening the success metric will keep producing accounts that balance while the conflicts beneath them do not.

title:
Does Economic Freedom Cause Prosperity?
Global Counterfactual Evidence on Growth, Distribution, Health, Productivity, and the State

detail.title:
Does Economic Freedom Cause Prosperity?
Global Counterfactual Evidence on Growth, Distribution, Health, Productivity, and the State

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study. The research relies exclusively on publicly available, secondary, aggregate country-level data and does not involve human participants, interventions, personally identifiable information, or individual-level confidential data.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. The research was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: This paper asks whether changes in economic freedom causally affect growth, distribution, poverty, health, productivity, and economic complexity, and whether any apparent effect is better attributed to government size, state capacity, or public-service efficiency. A harmonized global panel combines Economic Freedom of the World with World Development Indicators, Penn World Table 11.0, Maddison Project Database 2023, Global Macro Database, Heritage economic-freedom measures, economic complexity, IMF action-based fiscal consolidations, and commodity prices. Identification is treated as a competition among country/year fixed-effect local projections, exact-calendar leads and lags, abrupt increases and reversals, threshold sweeps, matching, synthetic controls, narrative fiscal shocks, component decompositions, state-size-capacity interactions, panel double/debiased machine learning, multi-treatment DML, AIPW, R-learning, nonlinear and quantile diagnostics, randomized index weights, cluster-bootstrap rankings, alternative state measurements, influence analysis, measurement perturbation, two-way and dependence-robust covariance, wild-cluster inference, country trends, temporal placebos, cyclic shifts, block and region-year randomization, restricted cluster sign flips, and BH/Holm/Bonferroni/max-𝑇 multiplicity control. The transparent three-year income estimate is positive but fragile: 0.0163 with country-clustered 𝑝 = 0.105, two-way-clustered 𝑝 = 0.216, 999-draw wild-cluster 𝑝 = 0.107, and 1,999-draw restricted cluster sign-flip 𝑝 = 0.088; country-specific linear trends reduce the coefficient to 0.0016 (𝑝 = 0.789). The decomposition is sharper. Legal/property institutions have coefficient 0.0797 and max-𝑇 𝑝 = 0.001, regulation 0.0284 and max-𝑇 𝑝 = 0.002, while size of government is-0.0060 with max-𝑇 𝑝 = 0.796. Legal/property ranks first in 97.6 percent of country-cluster bootstraps, and randomized convex index weights weaken the aggregate effect as more weight is assigned to government size. Matched abrupt reversals are followed by income losses that remain negative under multiple support filters, whereas synthetic-control reversals are imprecise because only six eligible cases remain. State capacity is empirically distinct from state size and service efficiency; favorable smaller-government effects are concentrated in high-capacity states rather than universal. Distributional, health, complexity, and most broad welfare results weaken after multiplicity and cross-design comparison. The evidence therefore rejects both a universal "economic-freedom coefficient" and an equivalence between smaller government, stronger state capacity, and greater state efficiency; the most reproducible signal is concentrated in legal/property institutions and the avoidance of abrupt institutional deterioration.

title: Keynes at the National Mutual: Insurance Practice and the Theory of Long-Term Expectation

detail.title: Keynes at the National Mutual: Insurance Practice and the Theory of Long-Term Expectation
detail.abstract: Chapter 12 of the General Theory is its most institutional chapter, yet its account of longterm expectation is usually traced to Keynes's philosophy of probability or to observation of speculative markets. Drawing on the business papers in volume XII of the Collected Writings, this paper reads the chapter against Keynes's insurance appointments: the chair of the National Mutual (1921-1938) and the board of the Provincial (1923-1946). The failure of his 'credit cycling' policy and the board conflicts that followed his turn to concentrated holding supplied the institutional content of its central categories: convention, reputation and the fetish of liquidity.

title: Missing Skills and the uneven Incidence of AI Simplification
affiliations: University of Southampton

detail.title: Missing Skills and the uneven Incidence of AI Simplification
detail.abstract: A rapidly growing literature examines which workers and occupations are exposed to artificial intelligence (AI), who adopts it, and how AI affects productivity. Much less is known about whether AI will narrow or widen income gaps across countries. We study AI simplification, defined as the reduction in task-level skill requirements within occupations due to AI. Combining crosscountry worker skill-use surveys with LLM-based measures of pre-and post-AI occupational skill requirements, we measure missing skills before and after simplification. Missing skills are strongly priced in labour markets: workers whose skills fall below occupational requirements earn less, and skill deficits are penalised more heavily than skill surpluses are rewarded. AI-induced skill simplification is greater in occupations with higher initial skill requirements. Since occupational requirements are higher in countries with higher per capita income, these countries also experience greater simplification. The gains from reductions in missing skills and the broader gains from AI simplification, including gains to workers with surplus skills, are also greater in high-income countries because of differences in occupational composition. Claude use is higher where simplification is greater and lower where post-simplification missing skills remain high. These findings suggest that AI may reduce missing skills while widening income gaps across countries, with uneven adoption further amplifying this divergence.

title:
Generative Value Cycle Theory

A Generative Theory Integrating Life, Cognition, Subjectivity, Education, and AI

detail.title:
Generative Value Cycle Theory

A Generative Theory Integrating Life, Cognition, Subjectivity, Education, and AI
detail.abstract: This study proposes Generative Value Cycle Theory, an integrative framework connecting life, value, questioning, understanding, subjectivity, time, education, and AI. The theory begins with life as a self-renewing system and derives value as an adaptive evaluative mechanism, questions as value-directed exploration, and understanding as the reorganization of knowledge structures. These processes form a recursive cycle in which understanding updates value and generates new questions. The study further defines the subject not as a fixed entity, but as the self-organizing process that sustains this cycle. On this basis, time, education, and AI are conceptualized as environmental conditions that enable, cultivate, and extend the cycle. AI, in particular, is positioned not as an autonomous subject but as an intellectual system that expands human reasoning and supports value updating. By integrating these concepts under a common generative principle, this study offers a cross-disciplinary theoretical framework for understanding human cognition, subjectivity, education, and human–AI interaction.

title: A Right to Delegate to AI: The Regulatory Safety Halo and the Acceleration of Agentic Consumer Markets

detail.title: A Right to Delegate to AI: The Regulatory Safety Halo and the Acceleration of Agentic Consumer Markets
detail.abstract: The European Law Institute's Guiding Principles and Model Rules on Digital Assistants for Consumer Contracts (DACC) propose a consumer right to use a digital assistant in business-to-consumer contractual relations. The DACC's broad definition encompasses consumer AI agents: applications that interpret consumer objectives and exercise discretion over transactional actions. The right would recognise agent use as a protected form of market participation, rather than merely preserve consumer protection when an assistant is used. This article examines two concerns. First, legal recognition and accompanying safeguards may create a regulatory safety halo, leading consumers to overestimate agents' technical reliability and the effectiveness of remedies for unwanted outcomes. Second, recognition may accelerate agentic consumer markets, disproportionately benefiting incumbents in adjacent digital markets and promoting concentration and private rulemaking, to which the DMA and EU competition law provide only partial responses. The article argues that legislation should determine the essential rules governing delegation and market contestability before recognising a general right to use a digital assistant encompassing consumer agents. Technical implementation should promote interoperability and contestability, constrain the normative choices left to standardisation bodies, and mitigate the legitimacy deficiencies of the existing European standardisation process.

title: What Can Be Identified from Satellite PM2.5? Evidence from 2.9 Million African Births
affiliations: Keio University

detail.title: What Can Be Identified from Satellite PM2.5? Evidence from 2.9 Million African Births

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by an academic fund of Keio University.

detail.abstract: In Africa, where ground monitors are scarce, studies of air pollution and health assign exposure from gridded satellite products distributed on a 0.01 degree grid. However, grid spacing is a choice about file format, and it need not be the scale at which the estimates carry independent information. We measure that scale in three ways. First, using the products' own fields, we find that the spatial variance they contain is not resolved below about 56 km. This figure is almost the same in regions whose monitor densities differ by two orders of magnitude. Second, using every usable ground monitor in the public archive, we find that the correlation between product and monitor is 0.89 for month-to-month variation at a fixed site and 0.87 for differences in level between cities. However, the correlation is only 0.03 for differences between sites a few kilometers apart within one city, where it cannot be distinguished from zero. Third, using 2.9 million births, we show that the robustness check the literature relies on, namely re-estimating with a coarser product, moves coefficients by only 0.32 standard errors, because the two exposure series are nearly the same variable. Finally, we estimate health effects using the one contrast the data measure. We find that none of 22 outcomes survives a multiple-testing correction, although the design has power to detect effects five times smaller than the published benchmark.

title: Ambiguity and the Supply of Cyber Reinsurance Capacity

detail.title: Ambiguity and the Supply of Cyber Reinsurance Capacity
detail.abstract: Primary insurers cede roughly half of cyber premium to reinsurers, yet dedicated reinsurance and retrocession capacity remains scarce, and the market's supply responses have run through exclusion clauses and trigger design rather than prices. I model reinsurance capacity supply when the accumulation-event probability is ambiguous: the reinsurer holds a set of credible loss models and evaluates commitments under smooth ambiguity aversion. Ambiguity adds a load that grows with commitment size and model disagreement; when solvency capital must cover the worst credible model, widening disagreement collapses supply discontinuously at unchanged prices and capitalrationing, not repricing. Exclusions that truncate the disputed region of the loss domain are worth strictly more than their reduceddistribution value, so narrower contracts support more capacity, and proportional treaties dominate layered ones for ceding a disputed book. Calibrated to catastrophe bond pricing, observed cyber spreads imply model disagreement that is modest relative to documented loss-model dispersion.

title:
Many Voices, One Model 
Synthetic Consensus and the Illusion of Independent Board Judgment

detail.title:
Many Voices, One Model 
Synthetic Consensus and the Illusion of Independent Board Judgment
detail.abstract: Boards derive value from plural judgment, yet conventional independence measures observe directors rather than the information infrastructures that shape their decisions. This paper develops a theory of synthetic consensus: agreement generated partly by shared large-language-model advice or common blind spots rather than independent evidence production. A common-signal model distinguishes procedural, model, and cognitive independence and shows how shared AI advice can correlate director errors while leaving formal board structure unchanged. A structured computational mechanism audit of five platform observations, six synthetic governance scenarios, and two prompt conditions yields 60 assessments. All actions were within researcher-frozen acceptable sets and all 12 tasks produced unanimous directional recommendations. Conservative coding identified one universal shared omission and one red-team threshold shared omission. Red-team prompting recovered four of 13 neutral omissions, introduced two new omissions, changed no action, and raised mean confidence from 88.07 to 89.93, or 1.87 points. The audit provides computational evidence for the mechanism at the advice layer; human uptake is a distinct external-validity question. The paper derives an independence-first governance architecture based on private pre-AI judgments, source-level provenance, evidence partitioning, adversarial verification, minority-signal preservation, and dependence-aware corroboration.

title: The Dollar Versus the Peso: Currency of Debt Choices among U.S.-Mexico Dual Residents

detail.title: The Dollar Versus the Peso: Currency of Debt Choices among U.S.-Mexico Dual Residents

declarations.funderStatement: Olin Business School, Washington University in St. Louis - PhD Program Office Center for Research in Economics and Strategy, Olin Business School, Washington University in St. Louis

detail.abstract: I study whether U.S.-Mexico dual residents borrow in pesos or dollars, using both theory and survey data. I attempt to understand the microeconomic and behavioral foundations of the actual and theory-predicted currency choice by households. I also attempt to reconcile the export- and import-related theory of currency choice proposed in the corporate finance literature with behavioral tests. Finally, I test the nominal uncovered interest parity condition established in McBrady & Schill (2007) in a household setting by analyzing if there can be any cost savings from borrowing in dollars over pesos and vice versa. Theoretically, I show that agents can have loan cost savings and maximize their utility of consumption by allocating their borrowing to either dollars or pesos based on what currency they consume in, currency path expectations, interest rates, and relative risk aversion. I find that generally, survey participants prefer to borrow in dollars, which is likely driven by the income and spending matching motivations and the country of primary residence and employment. This behavior is similar to corporations matching the currency of their revenue from exports and invoicing to the currency of debt. However, contrary to the theoretical predictions, where more risk averse individuals should be borrowing in dollars, I observe that higher relative risk aversion decreases the propensity of borrowing in dollars. This result is likely driven by the fixed vs variable rate survey design. Additionally, I find evidence that survey participants who mostly earn in pesos and are highly risk averse have a 6 p.p. lower indifference rate than those who are majority dollar earners.

title: From Green Logistics Readiness to Firm-Level GSCM Performance in Egypt: A Multilevel Synthetic Benchmark

detail.title: From Green Logistics Readiness to Firm-Level GSCM Performance in Egypt: A Multilevel Synthetic Benchmark
detail.abstract: This computational study validates a multilevel framework linking organizational capability and regional logistics readiness to green supply chain management (GSCM) adoption and sustainable performance in Egypt. The reproducible dataset contains 480 synthetic firms nested in 12 named industrial and logistics regions. The unconditional intraclass correlation was 0.438, indicating material between-region variation by design. In the random-intercept adoption model, organizational readiness (β=0.32), digital readiness (β=0.19), supplier collaboration (β=0.18), and human capability (β=0.11) were positive. The organizational-readiness × regional-readiness interaction was also positive (β=0.15). A zoneclustered performance model explained 54.0% of variance, with GSCM adoption as the dominant predictor. Results validate a cross-level analysis design; they are not empirical estimates of Egyptian regions or firms.

title: Where Climate Risk Enters Credit Ratings: Issuer Compression and Bond-level Sorting in China

detail.title: Where Climate Risk Enters Credit Ratings: Issuer Compression and Bond-level Sorting in China
detail.abstract: Credit ratings compress heterogeneous information into a small number of grades, but compression need not occur uniformly across issuer, security, and market layers. This paper examines where publicly observable climate-risk information remains visible in China's corporate credit-rating architecture. The analysis links a frozen universe of 1,468 interbank medium-term notes issued by 165 listed legal entities during 2010-2025 to reconstructed crosssectional issuer and bond-rating snapshots, 962 individual bond-rating records, three climate-risk measures, and conventional financial controls. Issuer grades are highly concentrated: 81.9% of rated issuers are AAA. Within the same 105 issuers, issuer-rating concentration exceeds modal bond-rating concentration by 0.0845 Herfindahl-Hirschman Index points, a positive gap in 98.5% of 5,000 issuer resamples. Issuer-balanced bond ratings retain still more category resolution. Yet issuance composition re-compresses the observable market: 85.4% of the 962 rated bonds are AAA, producing a raw bond-count HHI of 0.741. At the bond layer, AAA status sorts registered-location physical exposure, direct national emissions-trading-system coverage, and annual-report climate-risk language. ETS separation survives both Holm and Benjamini-Hochberg adjustments; physical and language separation survives the latter only. Climate variables nevertheless provide no stable incremental out-of-sample AAA classification beyond parsimonious financial information. The evidence therefore identifies a layered, associational transmission pattern rather than a universal climate penalty: security-level ratings can preserve climate-related differentiation even when issuer grades and issuance-weighted market observations remain compressed. The findings support legal-entity matching, security-level analysis, concentration monitoring, and transparent climate-credit overlays rather than mechanical downgrades.

title: Nitrogen-subsidence Cascade Theory: A Novel Conceptual Framework for the Feedback Mechanism of Accelerated Desertification via Groundwater Depletion, Biocrust Collapse, and Nitrogen Cycle Disruption in Dryland Ecosystems

detail.title: Nitrogen-subsidence Cascade Theory: A Novel Conceptual Framework for the Feedback Mechanism of Accelerated Desertification via Groundwater Depletion, Biocrust Collapse, and Nitrogen Cycle Disruption in Dryland Ecosystems
detail.abstract:
Desertification remains one of the most critical environmental challenges of the 21st century, yet
existing theoretical frameworks have failed to integrate geodetic processes—particularly
groundwater-induced land subsidence—with ecological and biogeochemical mechanisms driving
dryland degradation. Current theories focus on three feedback loops: soil degradation, land-
atmosphere interactions, and plant community shifts, but overlook the causal linkages between
subsurface aquifer depletion, physical soil disruption, biological soil crust (biocrust) collapse,
nitrogen cycle failure, and atmospheric dust-precipitation feedbacks. This paper introduces the
Nitrogen-Subsidence Cascade Theory, a novel five-stage framework that addresses this
fundamental gap.The cascade proceeds as follows: (1) Excessive groundwater extraction reduces pore
pressure in confined aquifers, triggering irreversible inelastic compaction. (2) Compaction manifests
as land subsidence, which physically disrupts surface soils through cracking, altered hydraulic
properties, and microtopographic changes. (3) These physical disturbances degrade biocrusts—
cyanobacteria, lichen, and moss communities that serve as ecosystem engineers in drylands—by
fragmenting their spatial continuity and disrupting moisture regimes essential for metabolic activity.
(4) Biocrust collapse disrupts the nitrogen cycle through three mechanisms: reduced biological nitrogen fixation (biocrusts contribute ~40% of terrestrial biological N fixation), increased nitrogen
loss via wind and water erosion (4–5 times greater than intact crusts), and altered emissions of
reactive nitrogen gases (NO, HONO, potentially shifting toward N₂O). (5) Bare, unstable soils
become intense dust sources; dust suppresses precipitation through cloud microphysical effects and
atmospheric stabilization, closing a self-reinforcing positive feedback loop that drives further
groundwater extraction.The theory's distinguishing feature is its integration of multi-scale processes:
geodetic-scale aquifer depletion and subsidence (kilometers to meters), ecological-scale biocrust
dynamics (millimeters to centimeters), and atmospheric-scale dust-precipitation interactions
(hundreds of kilometers). It proposes that desertification is not a gradual linear process but exhibits
nonlinear, irreversible regime shifts upon crossing critical thresholds—including the inelastic aquifer
compaction threshold, the biocrust collapse threshold, and the dust-induced precipitation suppression
threshold. Evidence from Iran—which experiences the world's highest subsidence rates (up to 35
cm/year), 1.7 billion m³/year of permanent groundwater loss, extensive biocrust degradation, and
intensifying dust storms—strongly supports the theory's predictions.A conceptual mathematical
model of coupled differential equations is presented, with stability analysis identifying groundwater
extraction rate as the primary control parameter. Exceeding a critical extraction value shifts the
system from stable to unstable equilibrium, triggering abrupt state transition. The theory has profound
implications for integrated water-soil management, emphasizing that surface interventions cannot
succeed without addressing subsurface groundwater depletion. Future research pathways include
empirical testing using remote sensing data (InSAR, GRACE, MODIS, GPM), model parameter
estimation, real-time monitoring system development, and comparative studies across global
drylands.

title: Universal Enrolment Is Not Universal Access: The Economics of Kenya's Taifa Care Reform
affiliations: Institute of Economic Affairs Kenya

detail.title: Universal Enrolment Is Not Universal Access: The Economics of Kenya's Taifa Care Reform
detail.abstract: Kenya's Social Health Authority enrolled 24.8 million members and disbursed KES 551.3 billion to 7,446 facilities in the ten months after Taifa Care launched in October 2024, while health-workforce density held near 13.8 workers per 10,000 people, roughly 31 percent of the WHO benchmark of 44.5. This paper argues that the binding constraint is clinical labor rather than money. Where the elasticity of substitution between financing and clinical staff is low, disbursement against a fixed workforce raises unit prices and queues rather than treated cases, and the entitlement is rationed by waiting, distance and informal payment. Three further claims follow: the contributory problem is base fragility and incentive compatibility rather than regressivity; the purchaser problem is a commitment failure rather than monopsony pricing; and delivery sits with the counties while revenue sits nationally. Each claim is stated as a testable prediction, with the series that would settle it.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Input-Output Analysis: Impacts on Backward and Forward Sectoral Linkages
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Unaffiliated Authors and Unaffiliated Authors

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence and Input-Output Analysis: Impacts on Backward and Forward Sectoral Linkages
detail.abstract: This article examines how artificial intelligence reshapes sectoral input-output relationships through backward and forward linkages, value-added generation, labor intensity, capital intensity, and the composition of capital services. It conceptualizes AI as a networked general-purpose technology that changes production within individual sectors while transmitting productivity gains, input demand, and systemic risk through interindustry supply chains. The framework combines input-output analysis, linkage indicators, value-added measures, labor-and capital-services ratios, and capital-composition metrics to assess how AI diffusion changes sectoral centrality and domestic value capture. The analysis indicates that AI strengthens upstream demand for software, cloud computing, semiconductors, cybersecurity, electricity, robotics, data systems, and specialized skills, while AI-enabled outputs from ICT, finance, logistics, manufacturing, health, education, energy, and professional services become productivity-enhancing inputs for downstream sectors. The article concludes that AI policy should be treated simultaneously as innovation, industrial, labor-market, competition, energy, and resilience policy because AI's economic effects are transmitted through production networks rather than confined to the technology sector.

title: Coalition Division as a Contested Garment: The Nucleolus, the Discipline that Sustains it, and the Protection of Small Partners
affiliations: London School of Economics & Political Science (LSE) - Department of Government

detail.title: Coalition Division as a Contested Garment: The Nucleolus, the Discipline that Sustains it, and the Protection of Small Partners
detail.abstract: A coalition government must hold its division of office period after period, against each member's temptation to defect. We study this as a repeated game of imperfect monitoring. Read as a claims problem, coalition division is a contested garment (Aumann and Maschler, 1985). The parties claim more office than there is to give. The division that resolves the shortfall is the nucleolus, which protects small claims rather than scaling awards to them. A coalition's gain from defecting is its cooperative excess, so the monitoring sustains the garment division. What the monitoring sets, through the parties' demand game, is the size of the over-claim. That fixes how far the division breaks from Gamson's proportional law. The break appears as a kink in the schedule of shares, its lower slope exactly one half. Gamson is the perfect-monitoring corner; the contested garment is what imperfect monitoring leaves. The result is general: it describes how any monitored group divides a fixed prize.

title: The Pricing of Cyber Catastrophe Bonds: Evidence from the First Market Cycle, 2023-2026

detail.title: The Pricing of Cyber Catastrophe Bonds: Evidence from the First Market Cycle, 2023-2026
detail.abstract: Cyber risk reached the catastrophe bond market in November 2023. This paper assembles a census of all Rule 144A cyber catastrophe bonds issued to mid-2026 (eight transactions, ten priced tranches) and asks how the market has priced them. Benchmarked against the average multiple of expected loss across all catastrophe bond issuance in the quarter of issue, cyber tranches paid a mean premium ratio of 2.3: roughly twice the spread per unit of modelled expected loss carried by contemporaneous natural-catastrophe issues. Every tranche priced above its same-expected-loss benchmark (exact binomial p = 0.002). Nominal cyber spreads fell by roughly a third between 2023 and 2025, but the marketwide multiple fell as fast: benchmark-adjusted, the cyber premium shows no decay, and point estimates rise. Sponsors gained instead on composition margins: deal size, guidance execution and structure. Persistence is consistent with ambiguity about cyber tail models rather than a transient novelty load.

title: "Desertion of Personality Rights in Copyright: Legal Consequences and Public Interest Considerations."

detail.title: "Desertion of Personality Rights in Copyright: Legal Consequences and Public Interest Considerations."
detail.abstract:
This research explains the underdeveloped concept of "desertion" of personality rights and how it relates to copyright and is at the intersection of privacy, dignity, and commercial value of an identity. An individual's personality rights include their name, photograph, likeness, voice, and other distinctive qualities; thus, personality rights are both dignitary (protecting reputation and autonomy) and proprietary (the idea of persona having commercial value when used for advertising, entertainment and digitally).

Unlike copyright and trademark law, which have established statutory and doctrinal concepts for abandonment, waiver, or misuse, the concept of "when conduct of the rights holder constitutes relinquishment, non-exercise or desertion of their right to control over their identity" lacks development within the same contextual framework. The research will use a doctrinal and comparative methodology whereby statutory provisions, case law, and secondary literature will be reviewed across the jurisdictions of India, USA, UK and the EU. The research will document the historical evolution of rights relating to a persona from Warren and Brandeis' "right to be left alone" to Nimmer's "right of publicity" and will include a discussion of relevant case law relating to Indian rights jurisprudence, such as R Rajagopal v State of Tamil Nadu, and Justice K S Puttaswamy v Union of India, as well as key cases concerning personality rights including DM Entertainment v Baby Gift House; and Titan Industries v Ramkumar Jewellers.

title: From AI Spending Guidance to Grid Commitment: Disclosure Attrition and Tariff-Duration Mismatch
affiliations: ,  and

detail.title: From AI Spending Guidance to Grid Commitment: Disclosure Attrition and Tariff-Duration Mismatch
detail.abstract: An 80% or 90% minimum bill is not necessarily 80% or 90% protection over the life of a grid asset. This paper documents two linked losses in the conversion of AI investment narratives into infrastructure commitment: disclosure attrition upstream and protection-duration attrition downstream. We combine two independently assembled, hand-audited U.S. datasets covering 40 hyperscaler earnings events and 27 large-load tariff chains. Cash capital expenditure is observable in all 40 events, but numeric forward guidance appears in 14, comparable same-target-year revisions in nine, and a blind model supports positive AI attribution in only nine of the 14 author-coded guidance observations; no event reports a standardized AI-specific payoff. Among five evidence-complete tariff architectures, stated minimum-payment floors are 80% or 90%, yet their narrow discounted 30-year coverage ranges from 0.388 to 0.900 at a 7% discount rate. Excluding the single 30-year term option, coverage ranges from 0.388 to 0.773 because support expires before the assumed recovery horizon. The datasets are not transaction-matched and support no causal claim. Their joint contribution is a duration-aware measurement result: better disclosure can improve planning without creating security, while strong headline protection can leave substantial tail exposure.

title: An Overdue Farewell: A Case to Abolish Sections 40 and 41 of the Trade Marks Act 1999

detail.title: An Overdue Farewell: A Case to Abolish Sections 40 and 41 of the Trade Marks Act 1999

keywords: Section 40 of the Trade Marks Act 1999
Section 41 of the Trade Marks Act 1999

detail.abstract:
Sections 40 and 41 of India’s Trade Marks Act 1999 restrict the transfer of a trademark where multiple exclusive rights in the trademark would result. The genesis of this restriction can be traced back to developments in the early twentieth century in the United Kingdom.

A couple of considerations vied for legislative attention at the time. One was the clamour from trademark owners for a permissive regime that would allow them the freedom to deal in their trademarks and associated goodwill as they saw fit. The other was an apprehension that permitting trademark owners to freely transact in trademarks could deceive the purchasing public by creating uncertainty over the source of goods and services bearing those trademarks. Legislators in the United Kingdom took a piece from both sides of this conflict in drafting Section 7 of the Trade Marks (Amendment) Act 1937. Despite showing a keen eye for the demands of commerce, they arguably overcorrected in their anxiety to protect the purchasing public from deception.

This protectionist stance was abandoned by the United Kingdom under the Trade Marks Act 1994. In India, however, these restrictions on transfers of trademarks were, at first, passively received under the Trade Marks Act 1940, and have, ever since, been unconsciously retained, without ever fully justifying, in case law or practice, their stated purpose.

In this paper, I present a narration of the conception and application of these restrictions in the United Kingdom and their assimilation into Indian law. I then outline a case challenging the continued tenancy of Sections 40 and 41 in the Trade Marks Act 1999.

The case proceeds as follows.

It contends, first, that from the standpoint of the incentives of trademark proprietors, situations where multiple exclusive rights would be created in a trademark by an assignment or other transfer are not meaningfully different from the general operation of assignments without goodwill, registered user agreements, and licenses. These categories of cases should not be differently. The onus for preserving value in trademarks in all such cases should lie with their proprietors, and not with the Registrar of Trade Marks.

Next, from the standpoint of the purchasing public, the harms of being deceived by the creation of multiple exclusive rights in a trademark are often overdrawn, both in incidence and gravity. In modern commercial settings, the purchasing public is aware of and accustomed to the manner in which trademarks are disseminated at scale via assignments and licenses. This characterization, though, is simply absent from Sections 40 and 41. Moreover, the risk of distortion of message between a trademark and its purchaser exists by default, even in cases where the trademark never changes hands. Under this view, a change in source of a trademark is not inherently deceptive. Deception can and does occur when trademarks change owners but it is often transitory and tolerable in ordinary course.

Finally, it is apparent that, as they currently stand, Sections 40 and 41 are not fit for purpose. Their presence in the statute alongside fundamentally more permissive provisions that permit proprietors to devolve trademarks to secondary users is irreconcilable, the restrictions themselves are marked by glaring inconsistencies in substantive law and procedure, and their enforcement is delegated to a duplicitous, hollow set of powers fashioned for the Registrar of Trade Marks.

With their original impetus then unconvincing and now long gone, I conclude that it is time to bid an overdue farewell to Sections 40 and 41 of the Trade Marks Act 1999.

title: Rare Earth Elements Supply and Financial Markets: Evidence from High-Frequency Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Rare Earth Elements Supply and Financial Markets: Evidence from High-Frequency Analysis
detail.abstract: Rare earth elements (REEs) are bottleneck inputs in many value chains, yet there is little evidence on how firm-level supply disclosures are reflected in REE spot prices and in the financial market. I compile calendar-dated disclosures from major listed producers, align them with daily spot quotes, and construct a firm–metal news shock series within a high-frequency analysis. Event windows display flatter densities with heavier tails, but no systematic rise in volatility. Local projections indicate small, metal-heterogeneous level shifts that emerge quickly and persist for several weeks. I find no statistically significant effects on the financial market, neither for broad equity indexes nor for REE-intensive firms. The paper contributes a new event-time database news shock series for REEs and provides, to my knowledge, the first high-frequency evidence on how firm disclosures are reflected in REE spot prices and the broader financial market.

title: From Organizational Position to Executed Action: Terminal-To-Execution Operative Carryover in Human-AI Systems
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Organizational Position to Executed Action: Terminal-To-Execution Operative Carryover in Human-AI Systems
detail.abstract: Human oversight is often described at the point where an AI-generated recommendation is approved, communicated, or otherwise recognized as an organizational position. That endpoint leaves a second problem unresolved: what happens when the position moves into execution? An executed action can match a terminal organizational position while having been reconstructed independently downstream; an inherited element can remain visible in logs while no longer determining the action; and an authorized position can be partially implemented, transformed, or overridden at the level of a specific parameter. Existing provenance, implementation-fidelity, approval-integrity, and agent-actiongovernance frameworks capture important parts of this space, but they do not by themselves classify whether a substantive element of a terminal organizational representation remains action-bearing through downstream execution. This paper proposes Terminal-to-Execution Operative Carryover (TEOC), defined over two predicates: lineage L(e,a), which asks whether a focal terminalrepresentation element e has a supported derivation or influence path into execution a; and operative status O(e,a), which asks whether the inherited element or mapped descendant determines or constrains a focal execution property. TEOC(e,a)=L(e,a) AND O(e,a). The framework distinguishes operative inheritance from descriptive persistence, high content fidelity, independent reconstruction, mapped descendants, and exact approval-to-execution identity. A priority-aware exact-neighbor collision was followed by a predeclared adversarial model-blind test using 12 synthetic cases comprising 15 focal elements. Two independent cross-vendor language models agreed on 15/15 final TEOC classifications and 43/45 pooled L/O/TEOC codes. The two sub-predicate disagreements exposed localized scope ambiguities that were adjudicated without altering any final TEOC verdict. The result supports only synthetic model-blind reproducibility of the diagnostic logic. It does not establish human inter-rater reliability, construct validity, external validity, prevalence, or causal importance. TEOC is proposed as a narrow extension of representation-aware organizational AI analysis from terminal position to executed action.

title: Zoning and the American Suburb
affiliations: Northeastern Illinois University - Northeastern Illinois University, Students, Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia and

detail.title: Zoning and the American Suburb
detail.abstract: American suburbs are generally characterized by single-family neighborhoods featuring large lots, with few businesses or apartments. To understand the origins of this pattern of development, we construct the first panel dataset of suburban zoning maps and bylaws for a major American metropolitan area and ask how comprehensive land use regulation shaped the form of the suburbs of Chicago today. Our strategy identifies the impact of zoning using land that was undeveloped before such regulations were adopted. The typical post-zoning suburban neighborhood sets aside over 90% of land for single-family homes, but adopting the most diverse zoning we observe reduces the single-family share by about half, with most of this land redistributed to businesses and apartments in equal measure. Supply restrictions were also binding earlier than widely believed, and prewar minimum lot size regulations were associated with lots that were 20% larger than those that emerged from unregulated markets. Comprehensive land use regulation thus substantially increased the prevalence of single-family residential neighborhoods relative to the suburban form that would have prevailed without zoning, which would have featured more mixed uses and smaller lots.

title: Climate Policy Uncertainty and the Path to Net-Zero Emissions in Australia: Nonlinear Effects and the Roles of Renewable Energy and Energy Innovation
affiliations: La Trobe University

detail.title: Climate Policy Uncertainty and the Path to Net-Zero Emissions in Australia: Nonlinear Effects and the Roles of Renewable Energy and Energy Innovation
detail.abstract: This study investigates the relationship between climate policy uncertainty and environmental quality, while examining the moderating roles of renewable energy consumption and energy innovation in Australia over the period 2004-2024. The empirical findings indicate climate policy uncertainty initially increases CO₂ emissions. However, the relationship between climate policy uncertainty and CO₂ emissions is nonlinear and follows an inverted U-shaped pattern: at lower levels of CPU, greater policy uncertainty is associated with higher CO₂ emissions, whereas beyond the threshold level, further increases in climate policy uncertainty are associated with lower CO₂ emissions. Furthermore, the results indicate that the effect of climate policy uncertainty on CO₂ emissions is contingent on renewable energy consumption and energy innovation, with both factors mitigating the adverse environmental effects of climate policy uncertainty. Finally, the findings highlight the importance of accelerating energy innovation and the transition towards renewable energy to mitigate the detrimental effects of climate policy uncertainty on CO₂ emissions.

title: The Economics of AI Infrastructure. Demand Growth, Cost Decline, and Capital Recovery in a Gigawatt-Scale AI Industry. Lessons from Fiber, Mobile Broadband, Software Platforms, and the Chunnel
affiliations: WiseHarbor

detail.title: The Economics of AI Infrastructure. Demand Growth, Cost Decline, and Capital Recovery in a Gigawatt-Scale AI Industry. Lessons from Fiber, Mobile Broadband, Software Platforms, and the Chunnel

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.ethicsApproval: All information used is already in the public domain.
declarations.funderStatement: Internally funded solely by author's firm, WiseHarbor.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is driving one of the largest infrastructure investment cycles in modern technology history. Investment discussion focuses on demand: users, prompts, tokens, models, GPUs, data centers and power consumption. But demand can grow enormously while investment returns disappoint.

Drawing on my long-horizon forecasting work in transatlantic fiber bandwidth and mobile broadband markets, I distinguish between two different AI businesses: physical AI infrastructure and frontier-model platforms. AI infrastructure resembles other capital-intensive sectors such as submarine cables and other fiber networks, with large sunk costs, rapid technological obsolescence, utilization sensitivity, financing risk and exposure to first-owner versus second-owner economics. Frontier-model development more closely resembles software-platform businesses, where ecosystem effects including developer adoption, distribution, brand strength and winner-take-most dynamics can create substantial value.

This paper develops a 1 GW reference model incorporating capital recovery, power consumption, utilization, technological obsolescence and ongoing model-development expenditure. It finds that current AI pricing is substantially above modeled serving costs under central assumptions, but examines how expanding capacity, open-weight models, Chinese competition, falling costs and changing market structure could soon compress margins. Data center utilization emerges as a particularly important variable because most infrastructure costs are fixed or quasi-fixed.

Analysis based on my cost model suggests that AI may become dramatically more valuable to users and application providers while some infrastructure investors experience disappointing capital recovery. The central question is therefore not whether AI succeeds as a technology. It almost certainly will. The harder question is whether market prices remain sufficiently above fully absorbed costs to reward those financing the first wave of AI infrastructure investment and its continuing expansion.

title: Last Fifteen Minutes: Equity Options Volatility at the Close
affiliations: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (RPI), Hofstra University, University College Dublin and

detail.title: Last Fifteen Minutes: Equity Options Volatility at the Close

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: We compare the relative informativeness of SPX implied volatility measured at 3:45 PM versus the conventional 4:00 PM close. The comparison is motivated by the rise of 0DTE options, which makes the close both the standard valuation timestamp and the expiration boundary for same-day contracts. Using matched option-chain snapshots, we show that the two volatility surfaces has become less aligned in shape as 0DTE trading has expanded. We find that using liquid at-the-money short-maturity options, the 3:45 PM data (as opposed to the 4:00 PM close data) is a better predictor of next-day realized variance. It also improves GARCH/EGARCH volatility models. Next, we construct raw volatility surfaces and train Convoluted Neural Networks (CNN) for out-of-sample forecasting, using the entire surface. The 3:45 PM surface outperforms the 4:00 PM surface as a standalone input. But, combining the two surfaces is even better.  Forecasts using the entire surface significantly outperform traditional at-the-money based forecasts. They are comparable to conditional volatility models.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Rule-Based Decision Support System for Short-Term Trading: A Case Study on XAUUSD
affiliations: K. N. Toosi University of Technology and K. N. Toosi University of Technology

detail.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning and Rule-Based Decision Support System for Short-Term Trading: A Case Study on XAUUSD
detail.abstract: Financial markets, characterized by high liquidity and rapid capital flows, require reliable predictive tools to support trading decisions and risk management. This study evaluates several machine learning algorithms to identify a robust short-term price forecasting model and, based on these findings, develops a rule-based decision-support system for algorithmic trading. Using XGBoost with tailored feature engineering, the proposed model forecasts five-minute gold (XAU/USD) price movements over a one-hour horizon, achieving a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.49 and a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.11%. When operationalized as a complete trading strategy governed by a fixed-dollar-risk position-sizing rule, the system produced a cumulative net return of 130.62% ($13,062.38 profit on a $10,000 initial capital) over the January 2021-October 2025 period, with Monte Carlo simulation indicating a mean annualized return of approximately 30.7% and an 89% probability of annual profitability. These results highlight the model's effectiveness for data-driven investment and automated trading applications.
